summary: AstroKids: Lunar & Mars Outpost Trainer is an interactive STEM simulation game designed for kids aged 7–12 to experience real-world space engineering trade-offs. Players step into the role of a Junior Commander managing a Lunar or Martian outpost for 10 Sols under a strict 100 kWh daily energy budget. To keep their crew alive and thriving, students must balance critical life-support systems—Oxygen generation, Radiation Shielding, Hydroponic Food production, and Earth Communications—while accounting for real communication delays (1.3 seconds on the Moon vs. 14 minutes on Mars). Powered by real NASA open datasets, including NASA DONKI for live solar storm emergencies and NASA OSDR for space radiation benchmarks, the game turns complex space science into hands-on decision-making.
details: What It Does & How It Works: AstroKids: Lunar & Mars Outpost Trainer is an interactive STEM survival game designed for kids aged 7–12. Players take command of either a Lunar Artemis base or a Martian Jezero base for 10 Sols. Each Sol, players must manage a strict 100 kWh daily energy budget across four critical outpost systems: 1. Oxygen Life Support: Maintains breathable air levels for the crew. 2. Radiation Shielding: Protects astronauts from space radiation and sudden solar storms. 3. Hydroponic Food Production: Ensures steady crew nutrition and health. 4. Earth Communications: Simulates real-world signal delays (1.3 seconds on the Moon vs. 14 minutes on Mars), teaching students why autonomous planning is essential in deep space. Benefits & Intended Impact: Most space education materials are either overly simplified or too complex for young learners. AstroKids bridges this STEM gap by making engineering trade-offs tangible, fun, and consequence-driven. Students learn critical thinking, resource management, and real space science while experiencing how NASA engineers keep astronauts alive on other worlds. Creativity, Tools & NASA Data: We integrated real NASA open datasets—using NASA DONKI for live solar storm alerts and NASA OSDR for realistic space radiation benchmarks—to create authentic mission emergencies. For design, prototyping, and visual storytelling, our team utilized Prezi and AI-assisted design tools to build an accessible, kid-friendly interface.
